title: The junior operator in her third month: the caller names the time himself; no name taken, nothing summed up
purpose: Story S4, period P3. A caller who knows what he wants books himself in. Maya asks the right questions and says yes to his time, then writes the booking against a truck instead of a person and ends on 'see you then'.

customer.name: Dwight Sizemore
customer.note: His name is never said on the call: the booking is under 'Tacoma, 12:30'.

call.day: a working day of slot 6 in score period P3 (rule R6)

scenario.who_calls: A first-time caller on a break at work; he asks one thing at a time and does not chat.
scenario.wants: a price, then a slot on his lunch break
scenario.what_happens: Maya asks what the truck is doing and how old the battery is, gives the installed price, agrees to the time he names, says who will be at the counter, and hangs up without a name, a number or a summary.

facts.note: catalogue.json battery_replace, class truck, standard: 304.45 (a menu price; the battery scales with the class). She says 'right at three hundred and five'.

prices.said: right at three hundred and five

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Maya, how can I help you?
Yeah, what's a battery run for a Tacoma? Put in.
Sure, I can tell you that. What year's the Tacoma?
Okay. And what's it doing — is it not starting at all, or just slow?
Slow. Turns over real lazy in the mornin'. Yesterday I had to jump it off my wife's car.
Ooh. Okay. Do you know how old the battery is?
It's the one that come in it, far as I know.
Oh wow, okay, so it's — yeah, that's a good run for a battery. So for the Tacoma, installed, you're right at three hundred and five.
Three-oh-five. Alright. I take lunch at twelve. Can I run it by there about twelve-thirty today?
Twelve-thirty today? Yeah, absolutely! I'll put you down for twelve-thirty, and I'll be up front, so just ask for Maya.
Oh, like twenty minutes. You can wait on it.

applied.what: hesitations and restarts dropped; dropped g's and contractions written out
a number split, merged or changed
a backchannel said over the other speaker is lost
a stock phrase the recogniser put over the silence at the end
